summary: Jesus travels through the towns of Galilee preaching the kingdom, with the Twelve and several women He had healed, who support Him from their own means.
key_insight: Luke names Mary Magdalene and Joanna here, in Galilee, long before the cross. When they come to the empty tomb (Luke 24:10), the reader already knows them as women who had followed Jesus from the start.
story: Soon afterward, Jesus went through every city and village, preaching and bringing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God. The Twelve went with Him.

So did certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities. Luke names three of them. Mary called Magdalene had been set free from seven demons. Joanna was the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward. And there was Susanna.
With them were “many others who provided for Him from their substance.” Out of their own means, these women helped meet the needs of Jesus and the Twelve as they traveled from town to town.

scene.label: Women on the road
scene.text: Jewish teachers of the time did not normally have women traveling with them as followers. That women went openly with Jesus and the Twelve, and helped pay their way, was unusual and would have been noticed.

scene.label: Magdala
scene.text: Mary’s name most likely comes from Magdala, a fishing town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, a few miles north of Tiberias. A synagogue from the first century was uncovered there in 2009.

scene.label: Seven demons
scene.text: Scripture says only that seven demons had gone out of Mary, a sign of severe bondage. It never says she had been immoral. The Gospels remember her for her faithfulness at the cross and the tomb.

scene.label: Herod’s steward
scene.text: Chuza managed the household or estates of Herod Antipas, the ruler who had imprisoned John the Baptist. Joanna was a woman of standing whose home reached into Herod’s court. She may be one source of what Luke knew about Herod (Luke 9:7–9; 23:8–12).

witnesses.luke: Only Luke pauses here to name the women. His Gospel is full of women who receive Jesus, from Elizabeth, Mary and Anna to the widow of Nain and the forgiven woman. Luke promised an account drawn from eyewitnesses (1:2), and he names these women as people his first readers could know and trust.

seeing.reveals: The Son of God chose to live on the gifts of people He had healed. He welcomed women into His traveling company and let their giving carry His mission from town to town.
seeing.living: These women gave because of what Jesus had already done for them, not to earn His favor. The Lord who healed them let them share in His work. Let what He has done for you shape what you give, and count it an honor that He uses it.
seeing.ponder: What has Jesus set you free from, and what would it look like to place your own “substance” at His service?

preaching.big_idea: Those Jesus sets free follow Him and spend what they have on His mission.
preaching.watch_for: In the NKJV, one sentence runs from the end of verse 1 through verse 3: “the twelve were with Him, and certain women.” Luke sets the women beside the apostles as part of the same traveling company, and the sentence ends on their giving.
